    Is it legal today?

    For thinning hair, a receding hairline or bald spots: what slows the loss, what regrows hair, and what is only marketing.

    • Finasteride 1 mg · daily pill that slows hair lossFDA approvedon prescription

      A daily pill on prescription. It slows hair loss in most men by lowering the hormone that shrinks hair follicles.1

      A daily pill. Slows hair loss and regrows some hair in most men; not for women who may become pregnant.

      FDA approved for hair loss.

      Prescription, from an online clinic or your doctor. From $10/mo (generic, pharmacy coupon).3 Online clinics from $25/mo (Strut Health).1 FDA letter 20 Feb 2026

      Evidence in people: Strong: many trials in people · Needs a prescription

      Buy from $25/mo · 2 clinics
    • Minoxidil · scalp liquid or foam for regrowthFDA approvedno prescription

      A liquid or foam for the scalp, twice a day, no prescription. Helps regrow hair while you keep using it.2

      A liquid or foam you put on the scalp twice a day. Regrows hair for men and women; works while you keep using it.

      FDA approved for hair loss.

      No prescription, any pharmacy. From $10/mo.4 Online clinics from $50/mo (Winona).2

      Evidence in people: Strong: many trials in people · No prescription needed

      From $10/mo at any pharmacy, no prescription4

      A minoxidil spray mixed by a pharmacy, prescribed by an online clinic. Not FDA approved.5

    Is it legal today?

    FDA status checked 7 Nov 2026

    Injectable peptides sold for hair are not approved for any use, and we found no human evidence for hair.

    FDA status of the peptides on this page, each with its source.

    PeptideStatusWhat that means
    BPC-157Not approvedHHS said on 30 Oct 2026 it does not intend to act against licensed pharmacies that compound it for one patient on a prescription, under 10 conditions; that is not FDA approval Source, 7 Nov 2026
    Finasteride (Propecia, Proscar)FDA approvedan FDA-approved product exists for hair loss FDA source, 31 Oct 2026
    GHK-Cu (cream or serum)Cosmeticcosmetics are regulated but do not need FDA approval to be sold 6
    GHK-Cu (injection)Not approvedby injection, its nomination for pharmacy compounding was withdrawn; by other routes, pharmacies may compound it while the FDA reviews it; no approved product FDA source, 19 Oct 2026FDA listings: "GHK-Cu (for injectable routes of administration)"; "GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes of administration)"
    Minoxidil (Rogaine, Theroxidil)FDA approvedan FDA-approved product exists for hair loss FDA source, 31 Oct 2026
    TB-500 (thymosin beta-4 fragment 17-23)Not approvedHHS said on 30 Oct 2026 it does not intend to act against licensed pharmacies that compound it for one patient on a prescription, under 10 conditions; that is not FDA approval Source, 7 Nov 2026

    Approved means the FDA approved a product containing it for a stated use. Not approved means no approved product exists; buying it for yourself is not a crime in the US, but nobody has checked what is in the vial. All substances

    Questions about peptides for hair loss

    What are the best peptides for hair loss?

    Finasteride and minoxidil are the only treatments on this page the FDA has approved for hair loss, and generic finasteride starts at about $10 a month. The options on this page: Finasteride 1 mg, daily pill that slows hair loss; Minoxidil, scalp liquid or foam for regrowth; Compounded minoxidil spray, pharmacy-made scalp spray; GHK-Cu copper peptide serum, cosmetic scalp serum; Injectable peptides sold for hair, research-use vials.

    Are peptides for hair loss FDA approved?

    FDA approved: Finasteride 1 mg and Minoxidil. Not FDA approved; pharmacy-made: Compounded minoxidil spray. Cosmetic, no approval needed: GHK-Cu copper peptide serum. Not approved for any use: Injectable peptides sold for hair. Each status has its source under "Is it legal today?".

    How much do peptides for hair loss cost?

    Finasteride 1 mg: from $10/mo (generic, pharmacy coupon). Online clinics from $25/mo (Strut Health, FDA warning letter 20 Feb 2026). Minoxidil: from $10/mo. Online clinics from $50/mo (Winona). Compounded minoxidil spray: online clinics from $45/mo (Keeps). Injectable peptides sold for hair: from $0.10/mg at 17 shops. Prices checked 8 Nov 2026.

    Do I need a prescription for peptides for hair loss?

    On prescription: Finasteride 1 mg and Compounded minoxidil spray. No prescription: Minoxidil and GHK-Cu copper peptide serum. Research use only: Injectable peptides sold for hair.
